items.title: Quasi-compact opens over a Galois extension are defined over a finite subextension and fixed by an open subgroup
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme X over k, a possibly infinite Galois extension and a quasi-compact open V of the base change, the lemma shows that V descends to a quasi-compact open over some finite subextension and that its stabilizer contains an open subgroup of the Galois group (statement lines 876-889). The proof obtains the descent from the general descent statement for quasi-compact opens along a finitely generated subalgebra, which gives part (1), and then observes that the Galois group of the extension over the finite subextension is open in the full Galois group, so its elements fix the descended open and part (2) follows (proof lines 891-895). The claim is H2: one descent input plus a one-line observation on the topology of the Galois group, with the passage from the subalgebra statement to the finite subextension being immediate in this setting.
